liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (3 reviews): Band stumbled a bit in Help>Slip because they had played that sequence only four times in eight years; Reviewer calls the Help>Slip>Franklin's sequence a trainwreck [15][16][20]
- **Blow Away** (2 reviews): Reviewer, at their first Dead show, singles out Brent's Blow Away as especially energizing; Reviewer notes Blow Away had some rough spots [17][26]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review): Reviewer singles out a nice Beat It On Down The Line [23]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Roughly fifteen-minute Bird Song soars and tops other 1989 versions, according to the reviewer [26]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer liked the unusual move from Help/Slip/Franklin's into Drums [26]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-10-22 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t02 Foolish Heart**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t03 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t04 Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t05 Queen Jane Approximately**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t06 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t07 Beat It On Down The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd89-10-22 s1t08 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-10-22.142576.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 175 min [1]
- **gd1989-10-22.167187.akg.c522.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 168 min [3]
- **gd1989-10-22.nak300.holtz.lmpp.97414.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 170 min [5]. Said about its sound: About nine seconds are missing at the tape flip in Drums [5]
- **gd1989-10-22.147644.nak300CP4.ebel.flac2496**: source not stated; 21 songs; 169 min [6]
- **gd89-10-22.sbd.brame.12188.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 156 min; rated 3.73/5 by 11 [13]. Said about its sound: Describes seven minutes of highly psychedelic MIDI weirdness, similar to other fall 1989 shows [24]

## Around the show

- Show was sold out, with about 25,000 attendees; ticketless friends waited in the parking lot [21]
- Before the show, pinkish-purple clouds hung in the parking lot sky; similar clouds appeared after Hurricane Hugo [23]
- Describes the show as decent, with a few musical flubs that are hardly noticeable [15]
- Reviewer says the band seemed tired after the Hampton, Meadowlands and Spectrum shows; the next night they rebounded [16]
- Reviewer attended Hampton and Spectrum shows too; found this night off in vibe, with the next night feeling refreshed [18]
- Reviewer sees no tiredness, calls it better than the following night [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-10-22.142576.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master (FOB)Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics @ 110 degrees, ORTF, Schoeps t-bar, hand held, chin high > Monster… [1]
- **gd1989-10-22.167187.akg.c522.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG C522 mics > Sony D5M [3]. Also: Ted Mattes' Schoeps source patches 3:10 of Space after Franklin's Tower and 1:43 of Drums [3]
- **gd1989-10-22.nak300.holtz.lmpp.97414.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz; transferred by Brian Green and SIRMick; source: Nakamichi CM-300s > Sony WD-5 > mac [5]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source from Holtz, released by Live Music Preservation Project; tape flips were crossfaded [5]
- **gd1989-10-22.147644.nak300CP4.ebel.flac2496**: taped by Taped & Transfers by Pete Ebel September 22, 2019; transferred by Pete Ebel; source: TS Nakamichi CM-300 CP4-> Sony D5-> Sony D6-> Cassette Master (Maxell XL-II's 90's) [6]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source patched with the Schoeps CMC4 Mk4 source for set one tape flip, set two tuning, flip and pre-encore deck pause [6]
- **gd89-10-22.sbd.brame.12188.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> ?> CD> EAC> SHN (EAC) [13]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1989-10-22 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1989-10-22-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [28]
